explanation: Retains the finite rounding slack when bounding executable sparse queries. The additive $9\rho\log2$ term preserves the integer-switch rounding loss in the finite logarithmic estimate.
theorem_title: Finite logarithmic bound for query terms
theorem_formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.CostLedger.queryTerms_log_bound {n j : ℕ} (hmu : 0 < _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Scales.mu n)
    (hj : j ≤ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Switch.terminalDepth n) :
    Real.log (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.CostLedger.queryTerms n j : ℝ) ≤
      (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Scales.mu n : ℝ) * Real.log 2 * (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Parameters.entropyRatio * (1 + _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Parameters.boxSaving - 2 * _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Parameters.bandShift)) +
        9 * _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Parameters.entropyRatio * Real.log 2 := by sorry
theorem_natural_language_statement:
Let input size $n$ have positive inner size $\mu$, and let $j$ be at most terminal depth. With entropy ratio $\rho$, box saving $b$, and band shift $\beta$, $$\log Q(n,j)\le\mu\log2\,\rho(1+b-2\beta)+9\rho\log2,$$ where $Q$ is the exact query-term ledger count.

Retains the finite rounding slack when bounding executable sparse queries. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
